title: Underwriting Bulletin: One FloodGuard Policy per Property Address
content:
**Rule.** A customer may insure several buildings or units under the FloodGuard Private Flood Policy, one policy per property address, up to 6 live policies. A live FloodGuard policy is one that is bound, in force or pending cancellation.

**Binding condition.** A FloodGuard policy is bound on a property address only when no other flood policy that is bound, in force or pending cancellation covers the same property address.

**Evidence.** Both conditions are judged on the company's policy records before the policy is bound: the property address and the status of each flood policy on file. The same property address is the correlation — a policy at a different address is a separate record and does not stand in the way.

## Condition — judgement — result

| Another flood policy at the same property address, status on file | Is it a live policy? | Does it stand in the way of binding at that address? |
|---|---|---|
| Bound | Yes | Yes |
| In force | Yes | Yes |
| Pending cancellation | Yes | Yes |
| Cancelled | No | No |
| Expired | No | No |

## Cases (hypothetical)

1. A hypothetical customer holds FloodGuard policies on five addresses, all in force, and asks to insure a sixth address with no flood policy on it. Six live policies is within the limit of 6.
2. The same customer, now with six live FloodGuard policies, asks to insure a seventh address. A seventh live policy would exceed the limit of 6.
3. A hypothetical address carries a FloodGuard policy that was cancelled after the building was sold. A new FloodGuard policy may be bound on that address, since the cancelled policy is not bound, in force or pending cancellation.
4. A hypothetical address carries a FloodGuard policy pending cancellation for nonpayment. No second flood policy is bound on that address while that status stands.
